name: Einthoven string galvanometer
summary: A very sensitive meter in which a fine wire moves in a magnetic field; sold to laboratories, it made the electrocardiograph practical.
description: Sensitive electrical measuring instrument in which a fine conducting string moves in a magnetic field; its motion can be observed or recorded optically, and it was adapted to electrocardiography.
tier_reason: A major reusable result, process or system within its field; broader multi-field or multi-generation dependence on this exact referent is not established.
why: Earlier capillary electrometers responded too sluggishly to record the heart's electrical activity faithfully.
